Using conventional log data, core analyses and elemental data, a free fluid model is developed over sections of reservoir and cap rock to establish zones of very good, good, moderate, poor, and very poor flow. A statistical approach is employed to establish elemental associations for discrete flow zones. The advantage of this workflow is that when a model has been defined for a field or basin, the acquisition of elemental data acquired during drilling can be used as a screening tool for both reservoir and cap rock identification. The elemental data can potentially be used to identify pressure ramp ups in overburden sediments.

title: Pressure reconstruction for airfoil gust response based on sparse measurement points
abstract: To address the complex unsteady flow phenomena encountered by aircraft in gust, traditional gust sensing methods, such as wingtip acceleration and root bending moment measurements, are limited by installation space, resulting in the acquisition of only localized and discrete flow information. It is impossible to sense the complete information of the flow field around the aircraft. Thus, the real-time gust pressure reconstruction models are developed in this study using compressed sensing based on proper orthogonal decomposition (CS-POD) and Gappy POD (G-POD), respectively. First, proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) modes are extracted based on computational fluid dynamics simulations under multi-frequency sinusoidal gust conditions, and reconstruction of the airfoil surface pressure under various gust scenarios is achieved through the solution of the temporal coefficients. The effects of the number and distribution of measurement points, as well as noise, on reconstruction accuracy, generalization capability, and robustness were systematically analyzed. Finally, wind tunnel tests were carried out to validate the engineering applicability of the proposed model. In contrast to G-POD, which requires five measurement points, comparable accuracy and robustness are achieved by the CS-POD with only three measurement points. In addition, wind tunnel tests validate the applicability of the CS-POD in real engineering environments. Despite the presence of factors such as model vibration and three-dimensional effects, the real-time gust pressure reconstruction model constructed using the CS-POD can still accurately reconstruct the surface pressure distribution of the airfoil.

title: Application of functional coatings in water electrolyzers and fuel cells.
abstract: Hydrogen, a sustainable energy carrier, plays a pivotal role in decarbonizing various industrial sectors. Key devices such as water electrolyzers and fuel cells enable a sustainable hydrogen cycle by producing hydrogen using renewable energies and converting hydrogen into electricity. The efficiency of these devices is primarily determined by electrocatalysts and other critical components like membranes, gas diffusion layers and bipolar plates. The dynamic and complex triple-phase reactions as well as the corrosive operational environments in these devices present significant challenges in achieving optimal performance and durability. This review not only summarizes recent advances in functional coatings but also elucidates the underlying mechanisms by which coatings modulate interfacial interactions and mitigate degradation. We further propose a roadmap for designing next-generation multifunctional coatings, emphasizing their potential to bridge the gap between laboratory research and industrial applications.
